attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, given in his list of facts he says Klein left out.

semantics.note: Keeps 'appears' and the naming facts. 'Appears' hedges only how the change is described. That Orion was released as GPT-4.5 rather than 5 is stated firmly, under 'The fact that'. This is a retrospective observation, not a probabilistic forecast.

contract.note: Reading 'downgraded' as a lower product name, not reduced capability, is the ordinary reading here. The contract keeps the tentative 'appears' and does not require proof of an internal decision. That is fair and does not stretch the claim either way.

evidence.note: TechCrunch, Dec 2024, summarising WSJ reporting that GPT-5 was code-named Orion. A secondary source, but it shows the earlier expected GPT-5 name.
Altman's Feb 12, 2025 post (a company disclosure) says GPT-4.5 is the model called Orion internally. That ties the same project to the 4.5 name. GPT-5 is redefined as a future integrated system.
OpenAI's Feb 27, 2025 release post confirms GPT-4.5 shipped as a research preview, before Marcus's post.

reviews.rationale: Reporting tied Orion to GPT-5 (e1). OpenAI confirmed Orion shipped as GPT-4.5 (e2, e3). Together these support the apparent drop in designation. Nothing shows the GPT-5 link was wrong or that GPT-4.5 was a different project. The roadmap change in e2 fits a repositioning and does not defeat the tentative inference.
